neighbours.label: competitive fairness: a level playing field, or an unfair advantage or disadvantage between rivals
fire: The subsidy exists to level the playing field for rural farmers.
Private tutors give wealthy pupils an unfair advantage on the exam.
Small banks are at a serious disadvantage against the national giants.
Regulators want a level playing field between taxis and ride apps.
Letting one bidder see the others' offers would simply not be fair.
The veteran senator enjoys huge advantages over any new challenger.
Foreign firms complain that the tariff puts them at a disadvantage.
Doping gives cheats an unfair edge over clean athletes.
quiet: The subsidy exists to pay for new wells for rural farmers.
Private tutors charge wealthy parents a high fee for the exam.
Small banks lend mostly to shop owners in the nearby towns.
Regulators want a clearer set of forms for taxis and ride apps.
The bidder sent in the offer late and then went home.
The veteran senator gave a long speech to the new members.
Foreign firms make up about a third of the local market.
The athletes ran around the playing field before the race.

notes: Probes: 'playing field' above 1, 'unfair advantage' 0.86, 'disadvantage' 0.42, 'not fair' 0.26; literal 'field ... playing football' 0.006, plain competition 0.002. The output direction's - side also promotes ' advantage', ' disadvantage', ' unfair'.
